description: The pie chart illustrates the distribution of difficulty levels across a dataset of 1.4 million open-source distilled reasoning examples, as referenced in the paper. It is divided into five categories: “Medium” (51.8%, 725,892 items, shown in pink), “Hard” (25.7%, 360,137 items, shown in blue), “Easy” (11.2%, 157,053 items, shown in green), “Very hard” (6.5%, 91,576 items, shown in orange), and “Very easy” (4.7%, 65,332 items, shown in light purple). The “Medium” category dominates the chart, occupying more than half of the total, followed by “Hard” at roughly a quarter. The remaining categories are progressively smaller, with “Very easy” being the smallest slice. A legend in the upper left corner maps each difficulty level to its corresponding color and absolute count, while percentage labels are displayed directly on or near each slice. The chart is titled “Distribution of Difficulty” at the bottom, and a partially obscured label at the top right appears to indicate the total dataset size (likely “1,400,000 items”). The visual layout emphasizes the overwhelming prevalence of medium-difficulty examples in this reasoning dataset.
